frame: supergalactic cartesian; directions also given in equatorial J2000 and galactic
interpretation: Amplitude ratios are the measured number-count dipole divided by the Ellis-Baldwin kinematic prediction for the CMB velocity. implied_velocity_kms is that ratio times 369.82 km/s, i.e. the speed required IF the whole excess were kinematic. That reading is deliberately literal; most authors regard it as a tension with the standard model rather than a measurement of our speed.

entries.label: CMB dipole
entries.surveys: 369.82 +/- 0.11 km/s; the kinematic reference all the others are divided by
entries.verified_from: standard value, quoted in Bohme et al. 2025

entries.label: Bohme et al. 2025, three surveys combined
entries.surveys: Negative-binomial estimator accounting for multi-component source overdispersion. Direction (RA, Dec) = (165 +/- 8, -11 +/- 11) deg; offset from the CMB dipole (5 +/- 10) deg.
entries.verified_from: fetched full text of the paper

entries.label: Bohme et al. 2025, NVSS + RACS-low only
entries.surveys: Same estimator without LoTSS-DR2; offset from the CMB dipole (8 +/- 10) deg. Direction not encoded separately - drawn along the combined-fit axis and marked as such.
entries.verified_from: fetched full text of the paper

entries.label: Wagenveld et al. 2023
entries.surveys: Poisson estimator on the same two radio surveys. Values as tabulated in Bohme et al. 2025, not read from the original paper.
entries.verified_from: secondary - quoted in Bohme et al. 2025

entries.label: Secrest et al. 2021
entries.surveys: Mid-infrared quasars; dipole amplitude about twice the kinematic expectation, direction approximately 27 deg from the CMB dipole. Ratio recorded as approximate.
entries.verified_from: web search of the published abstract

entries.label: Secrest et al. 2022
entries.surveys: More conservative test statistic on a deeper sample. Ratio recorded as approximate.
entries.verified_from: web search of the published abstract

entries.label: Dam, Lewis & Brewer 2023
entries.surveys: Independent Bayesian reanalysis of the CatWISE sample. D = (19 +/- 2)e-3, direction galactic (l, b) = (237.2 +7.9/-8.0, 41.8 +/- 5.0) deg.
entries.verified_from: web search of the published abstract

markers.label: Vela supercluster
markers.kind: mass concentration, hidden in the Zone of Avoidance
markers.notes: Position derived here from the published galactic (l, b) = (266, 1) at 189 Mpc/h. Mass approaches Shapley and exceeds Laniakea and the Great Attractor. The CF4-derived basin segmentation already in this page assigns that region to Lepus - there is no Vela basin, because CF4 barely samples the Zone of Avoidance: this layer carries ZERO catalogued galaxies within 20 Mpc/h of the Vela centre and only 239 within its 74 Mpc/h characteristic radius.
